newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans a 100,000-lev note in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans a 100,000-lev note in autumn.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to put into circulation in the autumn a 100,000-lev note, the largest denomination so far, to ease big payments in an inflationary environment, a government press official said on Monday.

"The interim cabinet approved today the design of a 100,000-lev note proposed by the central bank, which is expected to be put in circulation in September at the earliest," the official told reporters.
At Monday's spot rate of 1,500 levs to the dollar, the note would be worth $66.70.
The official said soaring inflation made higher denomination notes necessary to facilitate large payments and to cut the cost of maintaining the volume of money in circulation.
In February the interim government approved the design of a new 50,000-lev note expected to go into circulation by end-June.
The 100,000-lev note would be put in use when the 50,000 lev-notes cover six to seven percent of total money in circulation, the official said.
Money in circulation amounted to 337.6 billion levs as of April 11, the press centre said, quoting preliminary central bank figures.
The government also approved the design of a new 10,000-lev note due to replace the current one, which was put into circulation on December 9 and now is the largest denomination in use.
"It is expected that the 10,000-lev note would be the most widely used denomination in circulation in the next three years," the official said.
Under a memorandum of economic policies agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual inflation for this year was expected at 769 percent and at 14 percent for next year.
Monthly inflation for March was 12.3 percent and cumulative inflation for the first quarter was 452.3 percent. Annual inflation for 1996 was 311 percent.
